problem:
Consider the line $y=-x-4$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T?$

feedback.problem:
Consider the line $y=5x-2$ and linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the equation of the image of the line under the action of $T?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that the line $y=5x-2$ passes through the points $A(0,-2)$ and $B(1,3)$ since the coordinates of both points satisfy the equation.

To find the image of $A$ and $B$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing the coordinates of the points:

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 8 & -15\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective image points are ${A}^{′}(0,8)$ and ${B}^{′}(1,-15).$

Finally, we write the equation of the line that passes through ${A}^{′}$ and ${B}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-8 & =\frac{-15-8}{1-0}(x-0) \\ y-8 & =-23x \\ 23x+y-8 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
